title: Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) & Environment, Social and Governance (ESG) Assurance
outcomes: Explain SDGs and global sustainability reporting trends.
Describe integrated reporting and ESG evolution in India.
Perform assurance on sustainability information and consider climate in audits.

meta.exam_tip: Link ESG facts to both assurance standards (SAE 3000/3410) and financial audit SAs.

concepts.title: SDGs and global sustainability reporting trends
body: The UN's 17 Sustainable Development Goals (2015, target 2030) cover poverty, hunger, health, education, gender equality, water, energy, decent work, industry, inequality, cities, consumption, climate, life below water and on land, peace and partnerships.

Global trends: GRI standards for impact reporting, ISSB's IFRS S1 and S2 for investor-focused sustainability and climate disclosures, TCFD recommendations (governance, strategy, risk management, metrics and targets), and regional rules (EU CSRD, US and UK climate disclosure requirements).
Investors increasingly integrate ESG factors into decisions, making reliable sustainability information important.
concepts.analogy: Sustainability reporting is moving from voluntary to regulated.
concepts.work: IFRS S2 requires climate-related risk disclosures for investors.

concepts.title: Integrated reporting and ESG evolution in India
body: Integrated reporting explains how an organisation creates value over time using six capitals: financial, manufactured, intellectual, human, social and relationship, and natural.

India's ESG journey: National Voluntary Guidelines (2011), Business Responsibility Reports for top listed companies, National Guidelines on Responsible Business Conduct (2019), and the Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR) mandated by SEBI for the top 1,000 listed companies by market capitalisation.
ICAI initiatives include its Sustainability Reporting Standards Board, guidance and the Standard on Assurance Engagements for sustainability information.
concepts.analogy: Value creation is broader than profit — six capitals.
concepts.work: A listed company in the top 1,000 must file a BRSR with its annual report.

concepts.title: BRSR: structure and nine principles
body: The BRSR has three sections: general disclosures (company details, products, operations, employees), management and process disclosures (policies, governance for the nine principles), and principle-wise performance (essential and leadership indicators).

The nine NGRBC principles: ethics and transparency; sustainable and safe goods and services; employee well-being; stakeholder responsiveness; human rights; environment protection; responsible public policy advocacy; inclusive growth; and consumer value.

BRSR Core is a set of key ESG metrics (e.g. emissions, water, energy, waste, employee well-being, gender diversity) for which SEBI requires assessment or assurance for top listed entities in a phased manner, along with value chain disclosures.
concepts.analogy: Nine principles, three sections, and a core set needing independent checks.
concepts.work: Water consumption and GHG emissions are BRSR Core metrics.

concepts.title: Assurance on sustainability information and climate in audits
body: Assurance on sustainability information uses standards such as SAE 3000 (assurance other than audits or reviews of historical financial information) and SAE 3410 (GHG statements); assurance can be limited or reasonable.
Procedures: understand reporting boundaries and criteria, assess risks, test data collection systems, recalculate metrics, verify source documents and estimates, and evaluate disclosures.

Climate in financial audits: the auditor considers climate-related risks in assessing risks of material misstatement — asset impairment, useful lives, provisions, fair values, going concern — and reads sustainability information for consistency with the financial statements.
concepts.analogy: ESG numbers need the same rigour as financial numbers.
concepts.work: A company claiming net zero while expanding coal assets invites audit scrutiny.

summary: BRSR: top 1,000 listed; nine principles; BRSR Core.

viva.q: Name the three sections of BRSR.
viva.model: General disclosures, management and process disclosures, and principle-wise performance disclosures.

viva.q: What are the six capitals of integrated reporting?
viva.model: Financial, manufactured, intellectual, human, social and relationship, and natural capital.

viva.q: Which standards apply to sustainability assurance?
viva.model: SAE 3000 for assurance on non-historical information and SAE 3410 for greenhouse gas statements.

viva.q: How do climate risks affect a financial statement audit?
viva.model: Through impairment, useful lives, provisions, fair values and going concern, plus consistency of other information.

viva.q: What do the SDGs aim for?
viva.model: A global agenda to end poverty, protect the planet and ensure prosperity by 2030 through 17 goals.

cases.title: Elara Consumer Goods
cases.case: Elara, among the top 1,000 listed companies, publishes a BRSR claiming 40% renewable energy. Its auditor notices the plant using that energy was sold mid-year. Elara also faces new plastic packaging rules that may make some machinery obsolete.
